records.claim: There have also been reports of temporary changes in blood cell counts in some babies exposed to azathioprine or 6-MP during pregnancy. This appears to be more likely with higher doses, such as those used to treat cancer or prevent organ transplant rejection, or when the person taking the medication also has low white blood cell counts. Be sure your healthcare providers know you are taking azathioprine or 6-MP so your baby can be checked after birth if needed.
records.source_section: Does taking azathioprine / 6-MP in pregnancy increase the chance of other pregnancy-related problems?
